title: The map of work: O*NET work activities by hours of US work, with the raters' labels

method.hours: job-equivalents: OEWS May 2025 jobs of each O*NET 31.0 occupation divided across its tasks by importance (experiments/taxonomy/README.md, Weight), summed over all 15,600 weighted tasks; a task linked to several DWAs gives each an even share (an assumption: O*NET does not say how a task's time divides). Reads as hours only if every job has the same annual hours and time follows importance; importance varies little within an occupation, so in effect each job's hours spread almost evenly over its task statements
method.door: [n, door, mixed, doorman, split]: the distinct sampled tasks linked to the cell, by consensus (the raters' shared door label, or split where A and B differ). Unweighted: the sample is drawn with probability proportional to weight, so the count share estimates the cell's share of hours (approximately: certainty tasks and tasks linked to several DWAs count one each). null: no sampled task
method.spectrum: [n, position, physical, source, unsure]: position from closed (0: one right answer, reached one right way) to open (1: many of both), each task's answers and ways scored one 0, few 0.5, many 1 and averaged, then averaged over its raters (agreement gives the shared value, disagreement the mean of the two) and over the cell's tasks; physical is the share of those tasks both raters say need a body in the world, unsure the share only one rater says does. source s: the cell's sampled tasks; c: the cell has no sampled task, so the coverage task picked for it (chosen, not sampled: coverage_sample.json). GWAs use sampled tasks only. null: no labeled task
method.hours_nobody: the cell's hours times the share of its labeled tasks (the same tasks as spectrum) that need no body, for the chart's keyboard view. A task needs a body only when both raters say so, spectrum's rule; a task only one rater called physical is unsure, so it counts here as needing none and stays in the view (totals.sampled_body counts those tasks). Written only when every drawn cell has a labeled task (totals.spectrum_complete, and no DWA left without a sampled or coverage task); otherwise null in every cell, GWA and total, since a view over part of the labels would show part of a board and count the unlabeled rest as body work. GWAs and totals sum their cells
method.door_nobody: [n, door, mixed, doorman, split] as door, over the cell's sampled tasks that need no body (the hours_nobody rule). null: no sampled task, every sampled task needs a body, or the keyboard fields are left out (then every cell's is null)
method.color: spectrum once both raters have labeled every sampled and coverage task (totals.spectrum_complete), else door: the reading the labels can carry. The chart's default reading is door either way and nothing reads this field now; it stays for the file's stability
method.gwas: objects in order of hours: id, name, hours, door, spectrum (as for DWAs; source always s), hours_nobody, door_nobody, dwas
method.dwas: arrays in order of hours: [id, name, hours, door, spectrum, hours_nobody, door_nobody]. id is the DWA Element ID after its GWA's (c.7 under 4.A.3.a.2 is 4.A.3.a.2.c.7). DWAs no weighted task is linked to are left out (totals.dwas_zero)
method.examples: workmap-examples.json, same build: one task statement per DWA, in the order of the DWA rows here (GWA by GWA), each [statement, index into its occupations, door consensus]. The consensus is null where no task was sampled: the statement is then the DWA's coverage task (the weighted task carrying the largest share of its hours), chosen rather than sampled
method.credit: Includes information from the O*NET 31.0 Database by the U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration (USDOL/ETA), used under the CC BY 4.0 license, modified here (task statements weighted by employment and importance, summed into work activities, and a labeled sample). O*NET is a trademark of USDOL/ETA. Employment: BLS OEWS May 2025.
